newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine parliament gives '98 budget first approval.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine parliament gives '98 budget first approval.

text.p: Ukraine's parliament gave preliminary approval to the 1998 budget on Wednesday, even though the former Soviet republic is nearly six months late passing the budget for 1997.
"The budget is aimed at continuing economic reform and raising the effectiveness of the Ukrainian economy," the document said.
A projected deficit, inflation forecast and revenue and expenditure figures were not named.
The 1997 budget, expected to be passed by the end of the month, has been caught between the government and parliament.
Viktor Suslov, head of parliament's finance committee, said at a news conference on Wednesday that deputies would begin debating the budget next week.

Passage of the document, to be implemented in concert with nine tax laws, would mean fulfilment of one of 41 conditions Ukraine must meet to qualify for a $2.5 to $3 billion long-term credit from the International Monetary Fund.
